newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican prison official held after bloody battle.
newsitem.headline: Mexican prison official held after bloody battle.

text.p: Mexican authorities held the deputy director of a southern jail for questioning on Tuesday after a power struggle between rival gangs of inmates turned into a bloodbath in which seven died.
Seven inmates were killed and 57 were injured on Monday during a battle with guns and Molotov cocktails between the rival prison gangs in the southern Mexican city of Oaxaca.
Top church officials on Tuesday held a mass inside the jail to try to calm tempers.

Oaxaca state Attorney General's Office officials questioned Miguel Eduardo Snachez Valencia, the deputy director of the Santa Maria Ixcotel prision, on his possible role in the revolt, the Oaxaca state government said in a statement. It gave no more details.

Human rights workers said some of the inmates claimed he had helped arm one of the gangs, leading to the outbreak of violence. Prisoners were quoted on national Radio Red as saying authorities also controlled a drugs racket in the jail.
The riot raged for most of the day before police were able to regain control of the prison late on Monday.

For part of the day, dead or injured bloodied prisoners lay outside the hospital gates. According to a human rights worker who entered the jail, the dead were mostly smashed on the head with bars and clubs. But Molotov cocktails were also thrown and guns fired.
The fight was over control of a so-called "board of directors" that represented inmates before prison authorities.
Authorites said 35 inmates normally housed in Santa Maria Ixcotel had been transferred to other state jails as a security measure.
